## Chapter 5B Routing Decisions

| chunk_id | decision | question_ids | relevance | exclusion_reason |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| U0071 | **INCLUDE** | 5B.3, 5B.9 | Banxico's interest rate spread widened to over 6% vs. U.S. as a timely monetary response; pension funds cited as stabilizing domestic markets during foreign outflows — concrete policy response and stabilizing mechanism with measured spread. | — |
| U0072 | **EXCLUDE** | — | Adjacent context to U0071. Pension fund holdings (~20% of GDP) and estimated USD 7–10 billion annual purchases are background for the stabilization claim. No independently material policy action, measured outcome, cost, or distributional finding. | Topic overlap: background financial market context, no standalone evidence record |
| U0073 | **INCLUDE** | 5B.8, 5B.9 | Poverty rates quantified (rural 56.8% vs. 57.7% in 2018; urban 40.1% vs. 36.8% in 2018); basic food basket costs rising ~2% for rural and urban households (concrete distributional result). PACIC package announced May 2022 with fuel subsidies of MEX$395.4 billion / 1.4% of GDP — specific enacted fiscal measure with quantified cost. | — |
| U0074 | **INCLUDE** | 5B.3, 5B.8, 5B.9 | Fuel subsidy costing MEX$395.4 billion offset by MEX$397.8 billion windfall oil revenue (budgetary incidence outcome). Shadow-price fuel pricing formula codified in 2019 Presidential decree with four components — specific credible rule mechanism. Subsidies cut retail fuel prices by up to 30% in June; direct inflation effect quantified at ~2 pp (measured policy outcome against shock). | — |
| U0075 | **INCLUDE** | 5B.1, 5B.6, 5B.8, 5B.9 | Sembrando Vida (2019), Producción para el Bienestar, fertilizer expansion (5→9 states), Liconsa, Diconsa — enacted supply-side programs with specific objects. Scale ~0.3% of GDP. **Contrary finding:** Sembrando Vida land-ownership requirement likely excludes the poorest (distributional qualification). Fertilizer program emergency expansion documented. Price-freeze agreement with major retailers on 24 staples — concrete but unfunded measure with unclear impact. | — |
| U0076 | **INCLUDE** | 5B.10 | Manufacturing 50% foreign-demand-driven (automotive 80%); exports to U.S. tripled as share of GDP since NAFTA. Remittances rose from <1% GDP (2000) to ~4% GDP (2021). Regression quantification: 1% U.S. GDP change → 1.5% Mexico GDP change in 2010s vs. 0.2% in 1980s. Post-pandemic U.S. consumption shift from services to goods benefited Mexico. These are measured economic trajectory findings material to 5B.10. | — |
| U0077 | **EXCLUDE** | — | Countercyclical remittances and uncorrelated portfolio flows noted, but these are descriptive characterizations of observed patterns. No specific policy action, quantified cost, or measured distributional outcome attributed to the ruler under evaluation. | Topic overlap: background economic context, no material evidence record |
| U0078 | **INCLUDE** | 5B.4 | Dynamic regression and local projection methods applied to 2014 U.S. sanctions on Russia. Mexico exports to U.S. increased by USD 0.85 billion (0.07 pp of 2012 GDP) post-sanctions. Impulse response: Mexico nominal exports ~10% higher four months after shock. Specific empirical method and quantified trade diversion finding. | — |
| U0079 | **EXCLUDE** | — | Single methodological caveat paragraph acknowledging the analysis cannot attribute causality. Important qualification noted in decision for U0078, but does not independently contain policy action, measured outcome, cost, or distributional finding. | Generic methodological qualification with no standalone evidence record |
| U0080 | **INCLUDE** | 5B.9 | Food prices contributing roughly half of inflation overshoot above Banxico's upper target band — specific measured distributional driver of shock. Historical food-inflation episodes referenced (2008, 2017–18, 2011–13) for comparison. Weakness of economic slack at surge onset documented. Quantified comparative context for evaluating timeliness and targeting of shock response. | — |
